---
title: "USER-GUIDE-v001"
subtitle: "How to make, document and check AI-assisted projects"
---

## What this repository is for {#sec-purpose}

Each new project for AI-assisted work starts from the same base, so that people and AI agents find the same
things in the same places:

- `AGENTS.md`: the rules for every AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others) and every
  collaborator. It holds the project's rules and a copy of the **shared rules**, which apply to every project.
- `CLAUDE.md`: one import line, `@AGENTS.md`, so that Claude Code reads the same rules.
- `docs/`: the **project-docs Quarto book**: the SPECs, the guides, the TODO list and the plans. It is the quick
  way to learn what a project holds.
- `.claude/skills/new-doc/`: the skill that adds a document to `docs/`.
- `.claude/skills/pending-work/` and `.claude/settings.json`: the **pending work** list, things to do later. They
  are GitHub issues, and Claude Code shows how many are open when a session starts (@sec-pending).
- `.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json`: the template that the project was made from.

## Set up a computer {#sec-setup}

You need Dropbox (synced), Python 3.8 or later, git and Quarto. For `--github`, you also need the `gh` command,
logged in (`gh auth login`). This works on Linux, and in Git Bash on Windows.

1. Make sure that the Dropbox tools folder is on `PATH`. The tools folder holds `yrNewAiProject.sh` and
   `agents-init.sh`. On Linux, `~/.bashrc` has the line `export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/Dropbox/tools"`.
2. Run the setup script once:

   ```bash
   ~/Dropbox/_yrAiCoding/yrAiProjectTemplates/bin/setup-computer.sh
   ```

   It checks the `PATH`, and it adds an import line to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Then Claude Code follows the shared
   rules in every project on this computer. `setup-computer.sh --check` only reports.
3. Test: `yrNewAiProject.sh --list` shows the template versions.

On Windows, `python3` can be a Microsoft Store placeholder that does not run. The `.sh` commands then use `python`
or `py -3`.

## Make a project {#sec-make}

```bash
yrNewAiProject.sh --title "Photo Checks" --description "Reads photos of checks into a spreadsheet." ~/Dropbox/_yrAiCoding/yrPhotoChecks
yrNewAiProject.sh --type book --title "Python for Beginners" ~/Dropbox/_yrQuarto-master/yrPythonBook
```

The last word is the project folder. Its name is the project name. The folder must not exist, or must be empty,
or must hold only `.git`. The tool:

1. copies the shared template files, then the files of the type (a type file wins over a shared file with the same
   name);
2. fills in the project name, title, description, type, date and template version;
3. copies the shared rules into `AGENTS.md`;
4. writes `.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json`;
5. makes a git repository (branch `main`) and commits the files.

Then:

1. In `README.md`, write the "Getting started" section.
2. In `docs/SPEC-v0.1.0.qmd`, write what the first version must do.
3. Look at the books: `quarto preview docs` (and `quarto preview` in a book project).

Use `--dry-run` to see what the tool would do, with no change.

## The two types of project {#sec-types}

| Type | Use it for | What it adds to the shared files |
|---|---|---|
| `work` (the default) | Any work: programs, data, research, ... | A README for any kind of work |
| `book` | A Quarto book that you publish | The main book at the root (`_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`, `intro.qmd`), a README for a book, and `docs/PLANNING-v001.qmd` for the plans for the main book |

## The Quarto books of a project {#sec-books}

Each book is a folder with its own `_quarto.yml`. Give `quarto` the folder of the book:

| Book | Preview | Render | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main book (book projects) | `quarto preview` | `quarto render` | `_book/index.html` |
| Project docs (every project) | `quarto preview docs` | `quarto render docs` | `docs/_book/index.html` |

Run the commands from the project folder. Both previews can run at the same time. The QUARTO-GUIDE in each
project tells more.

## Add documents: the new-doc skill {#sec-new-doc}

Ask your AI agent for a new document ("make the next SPEC", "add a USER-GUIDE"), or run the script yourself:

```bash
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py                       # the next SPEC
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py USER-GUIDE --title "How to use the tool"
python3 .claude/skills/new-doc/new_doc.py --help                # all the options
```

- **A SPEC is the default type.** A SPEC has the version of its development step: `SPEC-v0.1.0.qmd`, then
  `SPEC-v0.1.1.qmd` (the default next version), or the version that you give with `--version`.
- **Other types:** `USER-GUIDE`, `DESIGN-GUIDE`, `TODO`, `PLANNING`, or any name in capital letters. They have a
  copy number: `USER-GUIDE-v001.qmd`. The next copy, `-v002`, is only for when you want to keep the old copy next
  to the new one.
- A new version starts as a copy of the newest version (use `--blank` for an empty outline).
- The script lists the new file in `docs/_quarto.yml`, above the older versions.

There are no PRD documents: a SPEC holds the requirements. The DOC-GUIDE in each project gives all the rules.

## The shared rules for AI agents {#sec-rules}

The shared rules are in `rules/AGENTS.md` of this repository, for example "every script has `--help`". They
reach the agents in three ways:

| Who | How they get the rules |
|---|---|
| Claude Code on your computers | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` imports `rules/AGENTS.md` (`setup-computer.sh` adds the line) |
| Collaborators, any AI agent, cloud agents | A copy in the project's `AGENTS.md`, between `<!-- begin shared rules -->` and `<!-- end shared rules -->` |
| A new project | `yrNewAiProject.sh` puts the copy in |

To change a shared rule:

1. Edit `rules/AGENTS.md`, and commit it.
2. In each project, run `agents-init.sh`. It replaces the copy, and keeps the project's own rules. Then commit the
   change in that project.

`agents-init.sh --check` reports a copy that is out of date. `agents-init.sh` also adds the shared rules to an older
project that does not have them.

## Add the templates to an existing project {#sec-existing}

```bash
yrNewAiProject.sh --add-to-existing --type work ~/Dropbox/_yrAiCoding/yrOldProject
```

The tool adds the template files and never changes a file that exists. If a template file (for example
`README.md`) exists already, it stops before it writes anything and lists those files. Then rename or move them,
and run it again. It makes no commit: look at the new files (`git status`), then commit them.

## Check a project {#sec-verify}

```bash
yrNewAiProject.sh --verify PATH                    # every template file is there
yrNewAiProject.sh --verify --check-content PATH    # ... and its text is as the template made it
```

`--verify` reads the manifest, and reports the template files that are missing. Extra files, and shared rules
that are out of date, are notes. With `--check-content`, it also reports each template file whose text changed
outside the filled-in values and the regions between `<!-- YRAI:BEGIN:NAME -->` and `<!-- YRAI:END:NAME -->`.
Files that you are expected to edit (the README, the documents) will differ. Use `--check-content` to see what
changed since the project was made.

## Put a project on GitHub {#sec-github}

Add `--github` when you make the project. The tool then makes a **private** GitHub repository with the folder name
(`gh repo create`), pushes the first commit, and makes the labels of the pending-work skill. To do this later, from
the project folder:

```bash
gh repo create --private --source . --remote origin --push
bash .claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh setup-labels
```

## Pending work {#sec-pending}

Pending items are things to do later, so that they are not forgotten. You don't use GitHub yourself: tell the agent,
for example "add a pending item: ...", "list pending", "let's work on #12", or "#12 is no longer needed".

- When a Claude Code session starts (and after `/clear`), a hook shows how many items are open, for example
  `Pending work: 12 pending items (3 high, 5 medium, 4 low)`. The list itself is not loaded, because a long list
  uses up the agent's context. Say "list pending" to see it.
- Each item is a GitHub issue in the project's repository with the label `pending-work`, a category label and a
  priority label. `_pending-work/pendingWork.md` is a saved copy, for when GitHub cannot be reached.
- A project with no GitHub repository yet keeps its items in `_pending-work/queue.md` until it has one.
- The details: `.claude/skills/pending-work/SKILL.md`, and `bash .claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh
  --help`.

To add pending work to a project that does not have it (one made from an older template, or any other project):

```bash
agents-init.sh --pending-work PATH
```

It copies the skill, and adds the hook to `.claude/settings.json` (it keeps the other settings). It never replaces a
file that exists. With a GitHub repository, then run `bash .claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh
setup-labels` once, and commit the new files.

## Options of yrNewAiProject {#sec-options}

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--type work\|book` | The project type (default `work`) |
| `--title TEXT` | The project title (default: the folder name) |
| `--description TEXT` | One sentence that says what the project is for (default: a TODO line) |
| `--version VER` | The template version (default: the newest) |
| `--github` | Also make a private GitHub repository, push to it, and make the pending-work labels |
| `--add-to-existing` | Add the template to a folder that has files; never change a file; no commit |
| `--strict-empty` | Refuse a folder that holds anything, even only `.git` |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be done; change nothing |
| `--meta-repo DIR` | Take the templates from another copy of this repository |
| `--verify PATH` | Check a project against its template |
| `--check-content` | With `--verify`: also compare the text |
| `--list` | List the template versions and their types |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show the help and stop |

Exit status: 0 OK; 1 `--verify` found a problem; 2 bad options, a missing template or a missing tool; 3 the folder
is not empty; 4 `--add-to-existing` would change a file; 5 git or gh failed.

## Change the templates {#sec-change}

1. A released template version does not change. A version is released when it has the git tag
   `templates-vX.Y.Z`. Projects record their version, and `--verify` compares them with it.
2. To change the templates, copy the newest version folder to a new version, for example `templates/v0.3.0/`, and
   change the copy. `yrNewAiProject.sh` uses the newest version.
3. Write a SPEC for the new version (`docs/SPEC-v0.3.0.qmd`), and update this guide.
4. Run `python3 tests/selftest.py`. It must print `OK`. Then render this book: `quarto render docs`.
5. Commit, and tag the version: `git tag templates-v0.3.0`.

## The retired yraiproject tool {#sec-retired}

Version 0.1.0 had a pip-installed tool, `yraiproject`, and one template, `genericTemplate`. `yrNewAiProject`
replaces it and keeps all its functions:

| yraiproject | yrNewAiProject |
|---|---|
| `yraiproject install TARGET` | `yrNewAiProject.sh TARGET` (also git, the shared rules, the type, `--github`) |
| `--template`, `--version` | `--type`, `--version` |
| `--allow-non-empty-safe` | `--add-to-existing` |
| `--strict-empty`, `--dry-run`, `--repo-root` | `--strict-empty`, `--dry-run`, `--meta-repo` |
| `yraiproject verify TARGET [--check-content]` | `yrNewAiProject.sh --verify [--check-content] TARGET` |
| `genericTemplate/v0.0.1` | `templates/v0.0.1/generic` (`--version v0.0.1 --type generic`) |

The old tool is in the git tag `yraiproject-final`. `--verify` also reads the manifests that it wrote.
